@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: Diff two model-visible skill catalogs into added / removed / changed entries
+---
+## What
+Add a pure value `SkillCatalogChange` (Operations/ or Registry/) built from an old and a new `[SkillMetadata]`. Both are filtered with the same predicate as the `skills` tool description list (`SkillsTool.make`, `context.visibilityPredicate`, default `SkillMetadata.isModelVisible`).
+
+It holds:
+- `added`: entries whose id is in new but not in old, in new catalog order
+- `removed`: ids in old but not in new, in old catalog order
+- `changed`: entries in both whose description differs after `SkillCatalogText.oneLine` (the text the description list actually shows)
+- `isEmpty`: true when all three are empty. A reload with no visible change posts nothing.
+
+A body-only change, or a change to a hidden skill, is NOT a change: the description list never showed it.
+
+## Why
+Request from the FoundationModelsACPAgent session (2026-10-19): a running session must learn when the catalog that the `skills` description listed has changed. Step 1 is knowing what changed.
+
+## TDD: failing tests first
+New `SkillCatalogChangeTests`:
+- [ ] identical catalogs → `isEmpty`
+- [ ] a new visible skill → `added`, in new order
+- [ ] a visible skill dropped → `removed`
+- [ ] a description edit → `changed`; whitespace that `oneLine` collapses → not changed
+- [ ] a body-only edit → empty
+- [ ] a skill that turns hidden (`isModelVisible` false) → `removed`; one that turns visible → `added`
+- [ ] a custom predicate is respected
+
+## Acceptance
+- [ ] Tests above written first and seen failing, then passing
+- [ ] `swift build` clean, full `swift test` green #skills
\ No newline at end of file

 position_column: todo
 position_ordinal: '80'
-title: Diff two model-visible skill catalogs into added / removed / changed entries
+title: Map the listed skill catalog to [CatalogEntry] for the Extras catalog compare
 ---
+#skills
+
 ## What
-Add a pure value `SkillCatalogChange` (Operations/ or Registry/) built from an old and a new `[SkillMetadata]`. Both are filtered with the same predicate as the `skills` tool description list (`SkillsTool.make`, `context.visibilityPredicate`, default `SkillMetadata.isModelVisible`).
-
-It holds:
-- `added`: entries whose id is in new but not in old, in new catalog order
-- `removed`: ids in old but not in new, in old catalog order
-- `changed`: entries in both whose description differs after `SkillCatalogText.oneLine` (the text the description list actually shows)
-- `isEmpty`: true when all three are empty. A reload with no visible change posts nothing.
+FoundationModelsExtras e6b2bf9 ships the compare and the text: `CatalogChangeNotice(kind: .skills, from:to:)`. It compares by name and description, and it gives nil when nothing changed. Order alone is not a change. It does NOT filter entries and does NOT normalize white space: the caller gives the entries exactly as the description lists them.

-A body-only change, or a change to a hidden skill, is NOT a change: the description list never showed it.
-
-## Why
-Request from the FoundationModelsACPAgent session (2026-10-19): a running session must learn when the catalog that the `skills` description listed has changed. Step 1 is knowing what changed.
+Thus this package only maps a catalog to entries: filter with the tool's visibility predicate, then map each skill to `CatalogEntry(name: id, description: SkillCatalogText.oneLine(description))`. Put the mapping next to `SkillsToolDescription` so that the description list and the notice entries come from one place.

-## TDD: failing tests first
-New `SkillCatalogChangeTests`:
-- [ ] identical catalogs → `isEmpty`
-- [ ] a new visible skill → `added`, in new order
-- [ ] a visible skill dropped → `removed`
-- [ ] a description edit → `changed`; whitespace that `oneLine` collapses → not changed
-- [ ] a body-only edit → empty
-- [ ] a skill that turns hidden (`isModelVisible` false) → `removed`; one that turns visible → `added`
-- [ ] a custom predicate is respected
+Delete the uncommitted `SkillCatalogChange` (Operations/SkillCatalogChange.swift). It is a second compare, which the request forbids. Rewrite `SkillCatalogChangeTests` against the mapping plus the Extras compare. Keep the cases that test the skills side: a hidden skill, white space that `oneLine` collapses, parameters and source not counting, a skill turning hidden or visible, and a custom predicate.

 ## Acceptance
-- [ ] Tests above written first and seen failing, then passing
-- [ ] `swift build` clean, full `swift test` green #skills
\ No newline at end of file
